gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured (not rated) usable AC output or a measured idle draw for any candidate station: StorageReview's Kill-A-Watt reading of 2.67 kWh out of the 3,014 Wh BLUETTI Elite 300 with an 8 ms switchover timed on a Quarch analyzer, The Solar Lab's 9.5 W idle on the Elite 200 V2 versus 15 W on the Elite 300, and Notebookcheck's 2,905 Wh (75 % of rating) from the Anker SOLIX F3800.
standout_why: Compared against Outage Authority (cited), the Reliance TF manual (cited, PDF unreadable via fetch), and PreparedStates. Outage Authority is the strongest rival: it carries NRC Canada's measured blower draw (490 W PSC / 284 W ECM) and LBNL model values, but every station figure is a spec with an assumed 85 % usable fraction (e.g. 'Elite 200 v2 (1,763)', 'Delta Pro 3 (3,482)'), and it gives no idle draw or switchover time. PreparedStates uses DTE Energy rule-of-thumb furnace watts and a hypothetical 1,000 Wh station with no product measurements. Neither names a lab that measured a power station. The furnace-side draw itself is not new (NRC via Outage Authority), so this angle is new and useful for the station column rather than pick-deciding on its own.
decides: Confirms the BLUETTI Elite 300 and Elite 200 V2 as the efficient picks for a cycling furnace load: measured 89 % (Elite 300) and 92 % (Elite 200 V2) of rated capacity delivered, with the lowest measured idle draws found (15 W and 9.5 W), which matters because a furnace at 40 % duty leaves the inverter idling 14 h a day (15 W × 24 h ≈ 360 Wh). It lowers the Anker SOLIX F3800 runtime below the page's 85 % assumption (Notebookcheck got 75 %: 2,905 Wh ≈ 12 h of PSC furnace at 240 W average, not 13.6 h), and raises the DELTA Pro 3 (Digital Trends averaged 3.7 kWh, ≈ 90 %, ≈ 15 h). The AC180's measured 950–1,030 Wh gives about 4 h of PSC furnace, confirming it as the marginal pick.

findings.label: Measured energy out, full to empty (StorageReview, Dylan Bryan)
findings.value: 2.67 kWh out; 3.49 kWh in from wall

findings.note: Kill-A-Watt on the output side, load not specified; 2,670 / 3,014 Wh rated = 89 % delivered; 2.67 / 3.49 = 76 % round trip (my arithmetic). PSC furnace at 600 W × 40 % = 240 W plus 15 W idle: 2,670 / 255 ≈ 10.5 h. Article dated 2026-08-27.

findings.source_title: Bluetti Elite 300 Review: 3014Wh, 2400W, and an 8ms UPS Switchover in a 58-Pound Box
findings.note: Workstation on the AC output, line power pulled then restored; BLUETTI's spec is ≤10 ms. Relevant only if the furnace is fed through the station's pass-through rather than a transfer switch.

findings.label: Measured idle draw, surge and efficiency (The Solar Lab)
findings.value: about 15 W idle, no load; 3,900 W surge reached; about 86 % efficiency; 2 h 44 min wall charge 0–100 %
findings.source_title: Bluetti Elite 300 portable power station review
findings.note: No byline or date on the page (copyright 2026); surge load type and duration not stated. 15 W idle × 24 h = 360 Wh/day lost while the furnace is off-cycle.

findings.label: Measured energy delivered and wall energy to recharge (StorageReview, Dylan Dougherty)
findings.source_title: Portable Power Meets Lab-Grade Reliability: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 Review

findings.label: Measured idle draw, efficiency and surge (The Solar Lab)
findings.value: 9.5 W idle; 94 % efficiency; 3,000 W surge held over 2 minutes
findings.note: No byline or date; load type for the surge not stated; The Solar Lab calls 94 % the highest efficiency it has seen in a power station. Lowest idle draw among the candidates measured here.

findings.label: Overload behaviour (CleanTechnica, Zach S.)
findings.value: shut itself off at 3,300 W against a 2,600 W rating; required a reset
findings.note: Article dated 2025-07-07. Also metered a 953 W portable-AC compressor (7.2 A at 119.7 V) starting and running 45 min from 100 % to 61 %, which is a motor load heavier than a PSC blower; no furnace test.

findings.label: Measured usable capacity (Notebookcheck, Marcus Schwarten)
findings.value: 2,905 Wh at about 260 W constant draw over about 11 h to shutdown at 1 %; 4,669 Wh from wall for 1–100 %; 42 dB at 1 m while charging at 3,000 W
